primarySourceInputs.observedPattern: Open pull requests and their head branches are public review surfaces and should be inventoried before claiming a repository is clean.
Remote refs should be listed by ref name and object ID as the public branch inventory, not inferred from the local default branch only.
Secret hygiene claims should distinguish current-tree local scans from full-history hosted secret scanning and alert status.
Security findings are strongest when they are rule-addressed and tied to Git refs, files, and lines.
Browser traces, DOM snapshots, network logs, videos, console output, and generated reports are data-bearing artifacts and should be blocked from public refs unless intentionally published.
Absolute local paths are disclosure risks and should be scanned as privacy findings on public repository surfaces.

evidenceChecks.label: default branch is present in remote heads
open PR discovery is usable when non-default branches exist
unexpected stale remote branches are absent
private local path and token patterns are absent from scanned public refs
browser capture artifacts are absent from scanned public refs
provider and live model calls remain absent

claimBoundary: This public GitHub surface audit inventories remote refs and open PR heads for privacy/security blockers only. It does not claim full GitHub secret-scanning alert status, full-history credential cleanliness, release readiness, production readiness, or external validation.
